A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StyloBench, the feature-inversion analysis, and StyloCheck. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original detector evaluations, feature-direction experiments, transfer-performance correlations, and a probe-count ablation.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds trained-detector evaluations, synthetic controls, intrinsic-dimension analyses, and fine-tuning experiments.

M1.justification: The inversion-direction eigenvector construction and StyloCheck's token shuffling, feature-based sample selection, and transferability scoring remain unchanged. Added RoBERTa fine-tuning experiments investigate mitigation without modifying StyloCheck.

E1.justification: Both versions use Stylo-Literary's seven authors, Stylo-Blog, the same five English M4 sources, and XSum probes. Additional experiments reuse these sources and the existing shuffled-text probe setting; no new substantive dataset or task coverage is established.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated RoBERTa and DeTeCtive detectors in Appendix B.3 and Tables 6 and 12–14, extending the comparison suite to training-based methods. V1 only discussed these approaches; its seven evaluated training-free detectors are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce supervised train/test splits, RoBERTa training budgets, and M4-only, literary-only, and mixed training conditions. Synthetic controls use three labeling conditions with 50 datasets each, containing 50 positive and 50 negative samples. Original training-free and StyloCheck protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds inverted-direction versus orthogonal/random controls, comparisons with within-M4 distribution shifts, lexical and sentence-level intrinsic-dimension analyses, and fine-tuning mitigation experiments. The existing probe-count ablation is retained, moving from Section 5.2.3/Figure 8 to Appendix D.4/Figure 12.

E5.justification: V2 newly specifies random seed 42 for RoBERTa and documents distributions across 50 datasets per synthetic-control condition. The original 100-experiment analyses and one-standard-deviation ablation reporting remain; no increase in their run counts is established.

E6.justification: V2 adds trained-detector scores, control distributions, distribution-shift comparisons, intrinsic dimensions, and fine-tuning results. Table 9, for example, reports mixed-training AUROC of 99.95 on Stylo-Literary and 71.94 on Stylo-Blog. Original benchmark scores are unchanged. Some new DeTeCtive summaries conflict with detailed tables, and the introduction reverses the class ordering despite unchanged Figure 3.

T1.justification: The inversion objective, eigenvector solution, quadratic-form derivations, and Rayleigh-quotient explanation are retained. New Equation 12 applies the existing Spearman correlation metric to M4 subsets; it introduces no new mathematical definition or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions remain. V2 softens the claim that feature inversion is the primary cause of detector failure to showing that it can undermine detectors, and explicitly positions StyloCheck as an early warning signal requiring no large-scale testing.

C2.justification: New Section 6 and Appendix E interpret inversion through lexical diversity and semantic coherence, distinguish it from ordinary distribution shifts, and discuss mitigation and limited transfer after fine-tuning. Appendix A.1 adds substantive dataset-design rationale. Existing language and deployment limitations are retained and elaborated.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies few-shot example selection, supplies RoBERTa hyperparameters and a DeTeCtive checkpoint link, and identifies encoders used for dimensionality analyses. It adds direct Blog-1K access information. Existing generator configurations and the project GitHub link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix E.2 substantially expands positioning against spurious correlations, domain generalization, adversarial robustness, invariant representation learning, and text reconstruction from embeddings, with corresponding citations. Section 2 also adds M4GT-Bench. Duplicate-reference consolidation is separate from these substantive additions.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, results narrative, generality analysis, and StyloCheck explanation are rewritten. V2 inserts a Discussion section, moves the ablation into the appendix, reorganizes experimental appendices, and expands the limitations discussion.

P2.justification: V2 adds control and distribution-shift plots and tables for trained detectors, dimensionality, fine-tuning, and hyperparameters. The original ablation plot moves from main-text Figure 8 to appendix Figure 12. Existing benchmark and example displays are retained with relocation, renumbering, and limited caption changes.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful controls and mitigation evidence absent from v1, but introduces substantive reporting inconsistencies. Table 6 gives DeTeCtive's Stylo-Literary average as 53.78, whereas Table 12's generator averages imply 69.00, undermining the near-random-failure interpretation. The revised introduction also reverses the class ordering shown in unchanged Figure 3. These evidential gains and reliability regressions prevent a confident judgment of net improvement.
